routes.label: Unit-vector norm identity and angular semicircle containment

changes.rationale: Use the conventional model of three independent uniform planar directions. For cyclic angle gaps a,b,c>0 with a+b+c=2*pi, unit-vector addition gives |u+v+w|^2-1=2*(1+cos(a)+cos(b)+cos(c))=-8*cos(a/2)*cos(b/2)*cos(c/2). The last identity follows by the explicit h070 difference formula and cofunction/parity identities. If all three gaps are at most pi, the product is nonnegative and the endpoint is at distance at most 1. If one gap exceeds pi, exactly one factor is negative and the distance exceeds 1. Thus failure is containment in an open semicircle. A containing semicircle has a unique initial one of the three directions, outside zero-measure coincidences or antipodal boundaries. For each specified initial direction, the other two independent directions both lie in its forward semicircle with probability (1/2)^2. The three cases are disjoint up to zero measure, so the desired probability is 1-3/4=1/4.

routes.label: Local factor sign, degree counting and coefficient comparison
Stationary polynomial zeros and repeated factor division

changes.rationale: Let P(x)=f(x)-(b*x+c), where f is the given monic sextic. It is nonnegative on all real inputs and has exactly three distinct real zeros r1,r2,r3. Repeated factor division gives P=(x-r)^m*Q near a zero, where Q(r)!=0. Polynomial continuity, already used in elementary finite-point limits, makes the sign of Q constant in a sufficiently small punctured neighborhood. An odd m would make P change sign; hence each m is even. The three roots therefore consume all six degrees, with multiplicity exactly two, and P=(x^3+u*x^2+v*x+w)^2. Comparing x^5,x^4,x^3 coefficients gives 2u=-10, u^2+2v=29, 2w+2uv=-4, hence u=-5,v=2,w=8. The cubic is (x+1)*(x-2)*(x-4), whose largest zero is 4. Its square expands to x^6-10x^5+29x^4-4x^3-76x^2+32x+64, so a=-76,b=-32,c=-64 are feasible and the graph is strictly above the line elsewhere. An independent calculus route uses that every zero is a differentiable local minimum: P(r)=P'(r)=0, so each (x-r)^2 divides P; the same degree and coefficient argument follows.

routes.label: Locate the centers, compute area, and factor its difference from the maximum

changes.rationale: Put beta=angle CBA=60 degrees+t. Since AC>=AB and beta<=90 degrees, 0<=t<=30 degrees. Set B=(0,0), C=(1,0) with A above BC. The sine law gives circumradius 1/sqrt(3). Direct side-line, perpendicular-bisector, altitude and angle-bisector intersections give O=(1/2,1/(2sqrt(3))), H=(1/2-sin(2t)/sqrt(3),(cos(2t)-1/2)/sqrt(3)), I=(1/2-sin(t)/sqrt(3),(cos(t)-1/2)/sqrt(3)). The vertex chain B,C,O,I,H is simple in the open interval: H,I,O have increasing x and y coordinates, with the other edges on the right and bottom; the endpoints are its continuous degenerate limits. Shoelace and the sine-difference formula reduce the area to K=(sin(60 degrees-2t)+2sin(t))/6. Let s=t-20 degrees, so -20<=s<=10 degrees. The exact identity 6*(K-sin(20 degrees)/2)=2*(1-cos(s))*(sin(s-20 degrees)-2sin(20 degrees)) follows by expanding with h070, cofunction identities and the printed cosine double-angle formula. The first factor is nonnegative, while sin(s-20 degrees)<0 and sin(20 degrees)>0, so the other factor is strictly negative throughout. Equality occurs exactly at s=0 in this interval. Thus the unique maximum occurs at t=20 degrees and beta=80 degrees. This proves the bound and equality without sine concavity, Jensen or trigonometric differentiation.

routes.label: Translate the six ordered regions and use cubic volume scaling
Compute the translated ordered tetrahedra by base and height

changes.rationale: Assume independent uniform coordinates in [0,n]^3. For n>2, split the cube into the six coordinate-order regions; all are congruent up to axis permutation and boundaries have zero volume. In the region x<y<z, the spacing condition is y-x>=1,z-y>=1. The translation (u,v,w)=(x,y-1,z-2) is a bijection to 0<=u<=v<=w<=n-2, preserving volume. This smaller ordered tetrahedron is similar to the original one with factor (n-2)/n. Its volume ratio, and hence the total probability across all six equal cases, is ((n-2)/n)^3. One can instead compute each ordered tetrahedron as one sixth of its containing cube, using pyramid base and height. For n<=2 the event has zero volume. For positive n>2, 1-2/n and its positive cube increase with n, as follows from inequality rules and a^3-b^3=(a-b)*(a^2+a*b+b^2). At n=9, 343/729<1/2; at n=10, 512/1000>1/2. Therefore the smallest integer is 10. Strict versus weak spacing changes only null boundaries.

routes.label: Restrict lattice pairs, compute rotated-square overlaps, and tile a unit cell

changes.rationale: The diagonal vector (0.2,1.4) has length sqrt(2), so S is a unit square with perpendicular unit side directions e=(4/5,3/5), f=(-3/5,4/5). Two distinct lattice points strictly inside one copy have separation less than sqrt(2); their positive integer squared distance must be 1, so they are horizontal or vertical neighbors. Three are impossible: two distinct unit lattice neighbors of one point are separated by sqrt(2) or 2, not less than sqrt(2). For a fixed horizontal pair p,p+(1,0), allowable centers form (p+S) intersect (p+(1,0)+S), since S is centrally symmetric. In the e,f coordinates the unit-square offsets are 4/5 and -3/5, giving intersection rectangle widths 1/5 and 2/5 and area 2/25. A vertical pair similarly has area 2/25. Distinct pair events have disjoint interiors because a square cannot contain three lattice points. Their union is lattice-periodic. In a unit fundamental cell, sum the areas of intersections with all integer translates of either fixed pair-center rectangle; translating each piece back partitions that rectangle, so the horizontal contribution is exactly 2/25 and the vertical contribution is 2/25. No integration or ergodic assumption is needed, only additivity and area-preserving translation. The 2012 by 2012 sampling square is exactly a union of unit cells, so the probability is 4/25=0.16. Centers for which a lattice point lies on the square boundary form finitely many line segments in the sampling box and have zero area; the strict-interior convention is respected.

changes.rationale: Possible movie pairs of distinct ages summing to 16 are {3,13},{5,11},{7,9}. The pair {5,11} is impossible because the 5-year-old stays home. If {7,9} went to the movies, among the remaining ages other than the home 5-year-old only age 3 is below 10, leaving too few for baseball. Therefore {3,13} went to the movies, {7,9} played baseball, and the remaining age 11 belongs to Joey. This is an actual deduction, not copying a given age.
